text:
Maria - Support: FYI ACME opened an escalation: streaming calls show very fast first byte (~30ms) but p99 total latency jumped to 12s over the last 24h. customer says non-streaming calls are fine. attaching their sample request and timelines.

Jamie (SRE): Ack. Can you paste their request (headers + params) and a few request IDs?

Maria - Support: pasted request id list and sample: req-9a7b6c, req-9a7b6d. They call /v1/generate with `stream=true` and max_tokens=1024, typical prompt length ~200 tokens.

Alex R: quick thought — "fast first byte, then long tail" sounds like chunk coalescing / buffer flush window issue at the edge. Did we recently push any proxy change?

Jamie (SRE): I'm seeing a small rollout of edge-proxy 2.3.1 started 12h ago, targeted at CA region. Rolling diff includes coalescing tweaks and a 5ms flush window (used to be 1ms). correlating metrics now...

support-bot: deploy-edge-proxy-2.3.1 started by ops@infra at 2467920000.

Sri P: Running p99 histograms for streaming vs non-streaming across the last 48h. Non-streaming p99 ~450ms. Streaming p99 jumped from 700ms -> 12s after 2.3.1 rollout. p50 unaffected.

Jamie (SRE): I pulled a couple of traces for req-9a7b6c: server-send-first-byte @30ms, then 11.6s idle before last chunk. The runtime shows model continued generating tokens (runtime logs show tokens emitted), but chunks weren't flushed to client. That points to the proxy coalescer holding bytes waiting for window.

Alex R: any differences between h2 multiplexed connections and SSE for this customer?

Maria - Support: customer uses h2 multiplexing through their SDK (we asked). They also said intermittent improvement if they reconnect.

Jamie (SRE): hypothesis: proxy coalescing interacts poorly with h2 stream flow-control + our chunk boundaries leading to middle-of-output waits. When model emits many small frames, coalesce timer groups them and keeps connection idle until window expiry -> long tail.

Sri P: Reproduced locally by force-instrumented client: open 5 concurrent h2 streams with small tokenized chunks; with proxy flush_ms=5 we see long p99 tails; with flush_ms=1 p99 drops to ~600ms. Repro steps:

```
# repro: simple curl h2 client sample
python reproduce_h2.py --host edge.test.redwood --num-streams 5 --token-emit-interval 2ms --flush-config 5ms
```

Jamie (SRE): Good repro. This matches production delta. The coalescer change was intended to reduce TCP/HTTP overhead but hurts interleaved small-chunk workloads.

Alex R: options: 1) Immediately rollback edge-proxy 2.3.1 in CA (fast but noisy), 2) patch config to set `coalesce_flush_ms: 1` for streaming routes, 3) provide customer workaround to disable streaming (use sync mode) or reduce concurrency.

Maria - Support: Customer asked for a fix ASAP. Which option is fastest?

Jamie (SRE): Fastest low-risk: patch config at the proxy layer (hot reload) to set coalesce_flush_ms=1 for streams route and canary to 10% then 100% in CA. I can push the config change now. Rollback is next if config patch fails.

Alex R: Also add a runtime fallback: if RPC detects long tail per-request >3s and model is still producing, bypass edge coalescer for that connection (flag to runtime). That needs eng-runtime but is medium risk/longer.

Sri P: For immediate mitigation, customer can call `?stream=false` or use the non-streaming endpoint; note this increases p50 but avoids the tail. I documented a short customer note.

Maria - Support: I'll send ACME the workaround and ETA. Please post runbook updates.

Jamie (SRE): Pushing hot config to CA canary now. Steps:
1) set `routes.stream.coalesce_flush_ms=1` in runtime proxy config
2) hot-reload config on 10% CA nodes
3) monitor streaming p95/p99 and error rate for 15m
4) if good -> scale to 100%, else rollback config

Alex R: I'll watch model/runtime token emission logs to ensure we aren't masking any other issue. Also add a metric for "coalescer_hold_time" to catch regressions.

support-bot: canary rollout started (10% CA nodes) by jamie_sre at 2468008120.

Jamie (SRE): Canary looks good after 8m: streaming p99 dropped from ~11.8s -> 650ms for the canary subset. No error spike. Scaling to 100% now.

support-bot: canary -> 100% rollout completed at 2468008520.

Sri P: Post-rollout aggregate: CA streaming p99 back to 700ms, p50 unchanged. Confirmed across h2 and SSE paths.

Maria - Support: Updated ACME: root cause = edge coalescing timer regression from recent proxy rollout; mitigation = hot-config patch rolled out in CA. They're pleased. Sending postmortem to them and internal ops.

Alex R: Action items:
- Alex: file runtime ticket to add coalescer_hold_time metric + defensive bypass (ENG-RT-452)
- Jamie: follow up with proxy team about revert of default flush_ms change (OPS-PR-303)
- Maria: customer-facing summary + repro we used

Maria - Support: assigning owners and adding to incident board. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jamie (SRE): follow-up note: we'll backport the config change to other regions as precaution and add a perf test for small-chunk streaming patterns in CI.

Maria - Support: I'll close the customer escalation once they confirm stability for 24h.
